author: The Italian Times
title: 82 Years Ago (1944), Reinhold Messner, Legendary Italian Mountaineer, Was Born in Bressanone
text:
On September 17, 1944, Reinhold Messner was born in Bressanone (Brixen), in the German-speaking province of South Tyrol, Italy. He was the second of nine children in a family of schoolteachers. His father introduced him to climbing in the Dolomites when he was young, and by his teens he was already making difficult ascents in the Alps.
South Tyrol became part of Italy after World War I, leaving a largely German-speaking population inside Italian borders. Messner grew up bilingual, shaped by this dual identity. He later pioneered “alpine style” climbing with Peter Habeler: lightweight, self-reliant ascents without fixed ropes, large teams, or bottled oxygen. It was a direct break from the heavy, military-style expeditions that had dominated Himalayan climbing until then.
The defining tragedy of his career came in 1970. With his younger brother Günther, Messner made the first ascent of Nanga Parbat’s Rupal Face, one of the tallest rock walls on Earth. Descending via the unfamiliar Diamir Face, Günther was killed by an avalanche; Reinhold survived, losing seven toes and several fingertips to frostbite. For over three decades, other expedition members accused him of abandoning his brother — a controversy that shadowed his early fame. Günther’s remains, found on the Diamir side in 2005 and confirmed by DNA testing, corroborated Reinhold’s account.
Messner went on to redefine high-altitude mountaineering. In 1978, with Habeler, he made the first oxygen-free ascent of Mount Everest; in 1980 he climbed it solo, again without oxygen. By 1986 he had become the first person to climb all 14 eight-thousanders, all without supplemental oxygen. He later crossed Antarctica and Greenland without snowmobiles or dogs, and the Gobi Desert alone. From 1999 to 2004 he served in the European Parliament; he has since founded the Messner Mountain Museum and published more than 80 books.
